The fourth emperor of the Mughal Empire, who ruled from 1605 to 1627. He was the son of Akbar and the father of Shah Jahan.

Born at Sikri, whose holy man had blessed Akbar with a son, he was named Salim. Akbar later built Fatehpur Sikri on the spot. As a grown prince he rebelled against his father, and in 1602 had Akbar's friend and historian Abul Fazl murdered. The two were reconciled, and Salim took the throne in 1605 as Jahangir, "world seizer".

  • In 1606 he had the Sikh Guru Arjan, who had compiled the Adi Granth, put to death.
  • In 1611 he married Nur Jahan, who became the real power at court, with coins struck in her name.
  • In 1615 the long war with Mewar in Rajputana ended in peace. That year the English ambassador Thomas Roe arrived at his court.
  • He lost Kandahar to Persia in 1622, and his son Khurram, the future Shah Jahan, rebelled.

Jahangir loved art and nature. His painters made detailed pictures of birds, animals and plants, and his memoir, the Jahangirnama, records what he saw with a naturalist's eye. He drank heavily and took opium. He died in 1627 and is buried in a garden tomb near Lahore.
sum: The fourth emperor of the Mughal Empire, who ruled from 1605 to 1627. He was the son of Akbar and the father of Shah Jahan.
